content.introduction: On February 9, 2026, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 52.27 points, or 0.10%, closing at a record 50,188.14, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.59% to 23,102.47 and the broad-based index lost 0.33% to end at 6,941.81. Oppenheimer upgraded Unity Software to outperform, and Raymond James upgraded Take-Two Interactive Software to strong buy. Meanwhile, Spotify's shares rallied 15% on better-than-expected results, and Japan's Nikkei 225 index reached a fresh record high.
body:
Also on Tuesday, Oppenheimer upgraded shares of Unity Software to outperform from perform and set its target at $38. That calls for 38% upside from Monday's close.

"We view the current risk/reward profile as favorable," analyst Martin Yang wrote. "We believe U will see accelerating revenue growth and margin expansion in 2026, validating its role not as a victim of AI, but as a primary platform for its deployment."

— Sean Conlon [...] The broad-based index lost 0.33% and ended at 6,941.81, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.59% and closed at 23,102.47. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 52.27 points, or 0.10%, posting a closing record of 50,188.14. The index had scored its third consecutive intraday record earlier in the day, a move that comes after it surpassed the 50,000 level for the first time ever last week. [...] On Tuesday, Raymond James upgraded shares of Take-Two Interactive Software to strong buy from outperform, pointing to a buying opportunity presented from the recent sell-off in shares due to fears around artificial intelligence disruption. The firm also kept its price target at $285. That implies 39% upside from Monday's closing level.

Investors also eyed earnings from big companies, including Dow component Coca-Cola. Shares in the soda company fell 1.5% after it posted disappointing net revenue.

Spotify's quarterly results beat expectations, fueling a 15% rally in the audio streamer's shares. Gucci owner Kering soared in Europe as traders welcomed signs of a turnaround at the luxury group. [...] U.S. Treasury yields inched lower and the dollar weakened after new data showed unexpected consumer weakness late last year. Retail sales were flat in December from a month earlier, stalling after robust growth in November and defying forecasts for a 0.4% rise. The data will be followed later this week by the delayed January jobs report and consumer-price index. [...] Japan's Nikkei 225 index closed at a fresh record high, taking its gains so far this year toward 15%. The market has been buoyed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's decisive victory in snap parliamentary elections held this past weekend.
